title: Make operational signals useful without exposing Ledger data

requirements.invariant: Every target event and metric has a stable registered identity, registered telemetry class, validated environment/build/contract scope, bounded dimensions or measurement, and a deterministic canonical representation before any adapter may emit it.

Session, Principal, Account, operation, and entity linkage uses typed domain-separated one-way correlation; emittable values contain no raw identifiers, credentials, URLs, notes, media, financial values, command payloads, provider messages, or unclassified text.

Environment/build scope and stable low-cardinality outcomes make queue age, sync lag, command rejection, decode failure, and reconciliation drift measurable without allowing environment confusion or user-content cardinality.

Telemetry contracts contain only Ledger and standard Swift values; provider SDK values, dynamic dictionaries, arbitrary field names, raw log messages, database paths, and transport errors cannot cross the target boundary.

Provider-free deterministic fixtures prove signal registration, exact allowlists, scope and correlation separation, canonical encoding, value bounds, and sensitive/unclassified refusal before a hosted adapter or production emitter exists.

items: TelemetryEventID, TelemetryMetricID, TelemetryDimensionKey and TelemetryDimensionCode are stable codes; signal definitions resolve one generated TelemetryClassID and exact allowed dimension/correlation sets.

TelemetryBuildScope is derived from a ValidatedLedgerEnvironment plus validated app version, build number and source revision; it contains environment/profile/contract versions but no endpoint, bundle resource, credential or user identifier.

TelemetryCorrelationFactory accepts only typed session, Principal, Account, operation or entity identity and produces a domain-separated HMAC-SHA256 digest; no raw identity is retained in TelemetryCorrelation.

TelemetryEvent and TelemetryMetricSample can be created only through TelemetrySignalCatalog validation, with sorted unique dimensions/correlations, registered values/units, bounded counts/ranges and a canonical-size ceiling.

TelemetryRedactionPolicy maps only explicitly safe classes to inclusion, protected classes to stable redaction, and identifiers/unclassified material to stable refusal without carrying the source value into a result.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This provider-free value/validation slice creates no Postgres table, view, function, constraint, index, telemetry sink, or retention schema.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No command/query handler or telemetry transport executes; later adapters may accept only validated envelopes.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, view, or function is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row or privileged function exists; future telemetry storage/retention requires a separate security slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: The catalog can describe Sync-health signals but defines no PowerSync Stream, subscription, row visibility, checkpoint authority, or local telemetry upload.

items: Validated event and metric values encode to canonical sorted bytes and reconstruct identically without a network, hosted destination, provider SDK or credential.

Equivalent reordered dimensions/correlations normalize identically; unregistered signals/classes, duplicate/disallowed keys, disallowed correlation kinds, out-of-range measurements, excessive fields and oversized envelopes fail atomically without a partial emittable value.
Correlation output is stable for the same key/scope/kind/typed identity but changes across environment/build/kind/key; no raw typed identity is encoded or displayed.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No attachment identity, byte, object, URL, media diagnostic, or upload/download behavior is introduced.

appMcp.notApplicable: This slice defines the target value contract only. App/MCP/handler emitters and parity tests opt in through later owning slices; current Firebase app/MCP logging remains unchanged and unadvanced.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No current Firebase/MCP log or production telemetry value is migrated; source logs are not target authority.

items: The initial technical catalog names stable platform-environment, contract-read, operation-status and sync-health events plus bounded duration/lag/count metrics under the generated telemetry classes.

Every validation/redaction/refusal failure is represented only by a stable safe contract code. No sink, retention policy, alert threshold, dashboard, runbook activation or production emission is created in this slice.

The contracts are additive target-only Swift code and tests, import no provider SDK, alter no current app project, contact no hosted service, and activate no telemetry emission or production behavior.

Future emitters opt in only after their owning slice and operational policy pass; reverting this foundation before cutover removes only target-only types/tests and no recorded user or operational data.

verification.expected: The initial event/metric catalog resolves only generated telemetry classes, rejects duplicate/unknown definitions, enforces exact dimension values/correlation kinds/units/ranges, and creates deterministically sorted bounded envelopes.

Canonical event/metric bytes round-trip offline; reordered safe fields normalize identically; opaque correlations are deterministic within and separated across environment/build/kind/key without encoding raw identity.

Credentials, URLs, notes, media, financial values, payloads and provider messages redact; identifiers and unclassified data refuse; unregistered/disallowed/duplicate/out-of-range/oversized candidates fail with stable codes and no partial envelope.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: Immutable pull-request evidence containing the unchanged implementation passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, the complete target test suite, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent technical-control foundation derived from the platform capability dossier. It stops before any telemetry SDK/sink, file/network persistence, Auth/provider resource, app/MCP/handler wiring, user/product event, alert/dashboard/runbook activation, migration, deployment, release, production emission, or cutover authority.
